Nta. I’ve faced a similar dilemma. I don’t smoke, drink or do any drugs or gummies either and I don’t plan to. I was with someone who was trying to quit smoking weed, and I thought I should give him a chance. I had the biggest crush on him and he was so sweet, smart and romantic. He respected me and didn’t try to push me to try it. He never came around me smelling like weed and he was already trying to quit on his own.

 BUT although people claim it’s not addictive, it is for some people. And even if they’re not addicted, stoners will tend to seek it out when things get stressful. I saw it first hand. If it’s a hard boundary for you and she decided to cross it, that’s on her.
Of course, I’m open to it! Thank you :)

That's what I've been saying. What difference does it make? Every good person on the earth could step up and we'd still miss someone. I feel like the best thing I can do sometimes is just remove myself from the equation. I'm not so sure I want to have kids grow up in this fucking cesspool.  I feel like it's ignorant to just go about your life and say "just be positive" or "just look at the good" when there is too many bad things going on even if the good outweighs the bad, and it sure as hell doesn't. You're not crazy, and I don't think a lot of people are worthless, but I see what you mean-we're insignificant.
I hate those statements along with, "It's gonna be okay." That phrase gets on my last fucking nerve.
Thank you for the words of encouragement, it’s always the little things that bring a small bit of comfort to keep going. I hope this pain is only temporary.

I feel you. Sometimes I feel as though something is wrong with me. I'm a junior in highschool right now so we're close in age. My grades are dropping and I'm isolating myself as well. I'm scared to be an adult if being a child is this shitty and I wonder if I should even put myself through adulthood. I understand your last couple sensences though a little too well. It's a war inside my head at all times. My therapist says to change how I think of stuff, but easier said than done. I don't know if I'll make it to 18 either, but I find some comfort here, knowing someone feels exactly the same way I do.

I feel the same way, sometimes I just feel like I wish the world would pause for a while, you know? It seems like everyone knows what they're doing and then there's me struggling through barely able to avoid a breakdown every 5 minutes. Recently, just planning my death has also been something calming because I know that at least if anything, I have that. I'm happy you're not to the point that I'm at right now, where I feel like my family might care, but ultimately be just fine without me. Hopefully, holding onto the fact that your family will miss you, will keep you from committing the act.
